summary.name: DockDoor
summary.one_liner: DockDoor is a free, open-source macOS app that shows live window previews when you hover Dock icons and adds Windows-style Alt+Tab window switching.
use_cases: See all open windows of an app by hovering its Dock icon
Switch to a specific window with Option-Tab instead of Cmd-Tab
Snap and resize windows with trackpad swipes
Browse folder contents from the Dock without opening Finder
Minimize, close or quit all windows of an app from its preview
summary.what_it_does: DockDoor adds window previews to the built-in macOS Dock: hovering an app icon shows thumbnails, a list or large previews of its open windows, including windows on other Spaces and displays and minimized or hidden ones. Option-Tab (or a configurable shortcut) opens a window-level switcher with search, and it can also appear above the Cmd-Tab app switcher. Trackpad gestures on title bars, Dock icons and the menu bar handle snapping, minimizing and switching, and Dock folders can be browsed via a popup. The page says it runs as a menu bar app, has no analytics or servers, and is notarized by Apple.
notable: Open source under GPL-3.0, with no analytics or usage tracking
Window-level Alt+Tab switcher for macOS, similar to Windows Alt+Tab
Gesture support for snapping, minimizing and switching windows
Separate paid DockDoor Pro app ($20 one-time) replaces the Dock entirely
caveats: Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later; Liquid Glass styling needs macOS 26 or later
Needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions
Some apps with unusual UI frameworks may show fewer windows or skip some actions
